thesis: A slow, warm, hypnotic liquid toy: wax blobs that merge and split in glowing liquid, lit from below, that you want to watch and poke.
job: open the page and see a lamp glowing at once
watch blobs rise, merge, pinch off, sink
turn the lamp on/off (heater) and watch it warm up or cool and freeze
adjust heat (speed), blob count, blob size
poke/drag a blob or shake the lamp, see it react
keyboard use of every control, state shown in the UI

principles: wax density vs liquid changes with temperature
heat from the base drives convection
surface tension merges and splits blobs
steps: temperature per blob: heats near bottom, cools near top
tricks: threshold the field for a crisp edge
low-res field upscaled is cheap and soft
blur+contrast (gooey filter) gives merging for free
tests: do blobs merge and pinch off?
does a cold lamp go still?
no blob stuck on glass forever

principles: light comes from below, glows through wax
tricks: per-pixel field with gradient colour at ~1/3 res then smooth-scale
rim light along edge by field near threshold

principles: one hot colour pair against a dark room
silhouette of the lamp is recognisable
steps: dark room bg with lamp-coloured light spill
tests: name it lava lamp at a glance

principles: every control changes visible state immediately

expectations: rise when hot, sink when cooling

kinds.name: classic rocket lamp
kinds.what: tapered glass, orange wax in yellow-ish liquid, chrome base and cap

descriptions: lamp is wide at bottom narrowing to top, then flare to a cap
blobs confined by the glass profile
behaviors: pool of wax at bottom when cold

descriptions: wax lighter and hotter at bottom, deeper at top
liquid darkest at top, brightest near bulb
one blob cycle takes 20 to 60 s at normal heat
behaviors: heat up: bottom blob lifts and neck stretches

descriptions: status text: warming, flowing, cooling, off
behaviors: drag blob to move, release and it carries on

anti_keywords.instead: tapered glass, merging field, glow, base and cap
slow thermal drift with long necks

checks: would a stranger say lava lamp at a glance?
do blobs visibly merge and split?
does the power switch warm up and cool down?
does every control change the lamp and its status text?
